location.name: Sioux Falls
location.institution: Fawick Park, Sioux Falls (bronze cast); the marble is in the Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence

object.medium: Scan of a bronze cast of the marble
object.description: Five metres of marble, carved from a block two sculptors had already given up on, by a man of twenty-six. David before the fight, not after it: the sling over his shoulder, the stone in his hand, his weight on one leg and his eyes on Goliath, the body a little too large in the hands and head because it was meant to be seen from below. Florence put it in front of the town hall in 1504 as the emblem of the republic and moved it indoors in 1873. The original has not been scanned under a free licence, but the moulds taken from it in the 1960s produced full-size bronze casts, and this is one of them, in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, scanned by a resident. The form is Michelangelo's; the surface is bronze.
facts: The block had been quarried in 1464 and left standing in the cathedral yard for forty years.
It was moved to the Piazza della Signoria over four days on rollers in May 1504, and stoned by republic's enemies on the way.
The Sioux Falls cast was a 1971 gift of the newspaper publisher Thomas Fawick, who gave a Moses as well.
